title: SPARQL performance
summary: A query-performance finding needs measured behavior and execution evidence.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.text: Record query text/version, dataset, engine/environment, relevant parameters, observed latency, and Neptune explain output where applicable.

sections.label: Proposed investigation
sections.text: Identify expensive execution behavior, test a constrained change on representative data, and compare correctness and performance.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: The optimization preserves expected results and improves the measured target. A query that looks complicated is not automatically slow, and local engine timing is not Neptune evidence.

catalog.applicability: Use this Neptune and SPARQL example when a query is suspected to be slow and you need measured latency, the query version, dataset, engine and Neptune explain output before proposing a change. Local engine timing is not Neptune evidence, and a complicated query is not automatically slow.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
